requirement:
The model-facing search and `finish_search` tool descriptions MUST give the
same selection guidance as
{cite}`requirements.authoring.search_accounting.instructions`.
rationale:
The subject requires the model-facing search tool descriptions and the `finish_search` description to give the same selection guidance as `requirements.authoring.search_accounting.instructions`. I read the guidance in that text as these points:
- Close every delivered search with `finish_search({search_id, used})`.
- Submission fails while a search stays open.
- Include a tag only if you used its snippet to justify your conclusion without an additional source read.
- Tags for entries whose source you also read may be omitted, and including them is harmless.
- Use `used:[]` when no entries qualify, including for an empty search.
- `finish_search` records dependencies and does not request more source.

The one test, `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[finish_search_advertises_the_accounting_schema_and_selection_rule]`, is marked `{test}` for the subject. It reads the real `definitions()` output and asserts on the `finish_search` description and on the `ripgrep` and `ast_grep` descriptions. The `references` tool is not covered, but its results carry no snippets or `search_id`, so it has no selection guidance to give.

**`finish_search` description.** The test asserts these phrases:
- "snippets you used to justify your conclusion without an additional source read" covers the inclusion criterion.
- "Entries whose source you also read may be omitted; including them is harmless" covers the subsequently-read case.
- "Use used:[] when no entries qualify, including an empty search" covers the empty-used and empty-search case.
- "Every delivered search must be finished before submission" covers the close-every-search and submission rule.
- "{search_id, finished:true}" and "no additional source is delivered" cover the point that it records dependencies and does not request more source.
- The `search_id` and `used` explanation and the JSON example cover how to call it.

It also asserts the exact parameter schema.

**`ripgrep` and `ast_grep` descriptions.** For each, the test asserts:
- "tags whose snippets you used to justify your conclusion without an additional source read"
- "Entries whose source you also read may be omitted; including them is harmless"
- "Use an empty used list if no entries qualify"
- "Before submitting, call finish_search"
- the tool-choice sentence

I read the descriptions in `fn[definitions]` and they contain these phrases. The wording is not identical to the required text, which is fine because the requirement asks for the same guidance rather than the same words. For example, "Every delivered search must be finished before submission" stands in for "Submission fails while any search remains open".

**Possible gap, not counted.** The search descriptions do not repeat "including for an empty search", and the test does not assert it for them. The search tools do state that "No matches returns an empty matches array" and that an empty used list is allowed when nothing qualifies. The `finish_search` description, which is asserted, carries the empty-search guidance. I do not treat this as a gap.

A change that dropped or contradicted any of the main guidance points in these descriptions would fail the assertions. The test is adequate for this requirement.

text: The model-facing search and `finish_search` tool descriptions MUST give the
The `instructions` field supplied under {cite}`requirements.authoring.search_accounting.first_result` MUST contain the following text.

Before submitting your assessment, close every delivered search with finish_search({search_id, used:[tags]}). Submission fails while any search remains open. Include a tag only when you used information in its snippet to justify your conclusion without an additional source read. Entries whose source you subsequently read with habeas may be omitted; including them is harmless. Use used:[] when no entries qualify, including for an empty search. finish_search records dependencies and does not request more source.
